items.html:
All six concepts fit direct WASM + JavaScript/TypeScript.

  • Draggable spheres: current exports support coupled scattering and exterior fields. An “uncoupled” comparison needs local single-sphere responses assembled with the correct incident phases; a small native helper would keep this clean.
  • Resonance strip: ready today. Group scattered coefficients by multipole order for dipole/quadrupole contributions. Electric-versus-magnetic labels additionally need the helicity-to-parity conversion.
  • Mode mixer: arbitrary regular-mode mixing is valid for a single expansion origin. For clusters, mix complete plane_wave() vectors so incident fields remain physically consistent across particles. Arbitrarily editing each particle’s local coefficients does not guarantee a realizable common incident field.
  • Core-shell suppression: ready with existing layered-sphere exports. Keep the exterior field masked inside the particle and compare against a clearly specified reference particle.
  • Chirality comparison: ready with material kappa and helicities 0/1. Label material chirality explicitly; the spherical geometry itself is unchanged.
  • Tap-to-optimize: later. Native derivatives exist, but WASM currently discards their residuals. This needs retained forward/pullback bindings and tested parameter constraints.

Your cached harmonic-phase animation is appropriate. One further distinction: sampled angular fields at a finite observation radius should be labelled accordingly, rather than presented as exact far-field radiation patterns.

items.html:
The existing core covers these paths. For the low-order demos, use vacuum embedding and reuse the current dense solve; no new numerical solver is needed.

  1. Incident, total and uncoupled fields

Normalize the direction exactly as ScatteringSystem::plane_wave does, then:

let k = direction.map(|d| Complex::new(k0 * d / norm, 0.0));
let polarization = plane::polarization(k, helicity, true)?;
let incident = plane::field_value(polarization, k, point.map(Complex::from))?;

Compute polarization once per incident wave, then evaluate all world-space points. For a coherent beam mixture, sum these complex fields with the same weights used to combine plane::expansion columns.

The correct exterior total field is one direct incident field plus the summed outgoing multipole field. Calling electric_field(a, points, false) on the complete cluster incident vector duplicates the incident field across expansion origins.

For the uncoupled comparison:

  • Build each local block with tmatrix::sphere(lmax, k0, &[radius], &[particle_material, Material::default()]).
  • Obtain the incident vector using plane::expansion(cluster_basis, vectors, polarizations, true). This already includes each sphere’s exp(i k·position) phase.
  • Apply each local block independently: b_i = T_i a_i.
  • Evaluate all outgoing contributions together with fields::field(..., Radial::Outgoing).

Keep coherent interference between the emitted fields. “Uncoupled” disables rescattering between particles, not interference. Zeroing off-diagonal entries of an already coupled T matrix is incorrect: its diagonal blocks also contain rescattering corrections.

  1. Scattering scores and multipoles

For one sphere/core-shell particle in vacuum, illuminated by one unit-amplitude plane wave, let a be its incident coefficients and b = T a:

[ C_{\rm sca}=\frac{\sum_i |b_i|^2}{k_0^2},\qquad C_{\rm ext}=-\frac{\operatorname{Re}(a^\dagger b)}{k_0^2},\qquad C_{\rm abs}=C_{\rm ext}-C_{\rm sca}. ]

These factors reproduce both committed single-sphere fixtures in a read-only probe. Dimensionless efficiency is Q = C / (π R_outer²).

Use waves::modes(lmax) to group coefficients by mode.l. The contribution of degree l is the same scattering sum restricted to that degree. Current pair ordering is positive helicity, negative helicity for each (l,m). Electric/magnetic coefficients follow the existing convention:

[ b_N=(b_+ + b_-)/\sqrt2,\qquad b_M=(b_+ - b_-)/\sqrt2. ]

Sum their squared magnitudes separately for electric/magnetic multipole bars. No additional special-function kernel is necessary.

For radius/material derivatives of C_sca, use g_b = 2b/k0², g_T = g_b a†, then SphereResidual::pullback(&g_T). It returns radii and complex epsilon, mu, kappa gradients. An efficiency objective additionally needs the outer-area derivative; a moving reference particle additionally needs its own derivative. A fixed reference and fixed outer radius make the suppression challenge simpler.

For clusters, do not use sum |b_i|² as total scattering. The existing Python contract includes coherent radiation overlap:

let overlap = basis::translation(
    basis.clone(), basis.clone(), ks, true, Radial::Regular
)?;

Then C_sca = Re(b† overlap.value b)/k0²; extinction retains the formula above.

Helicity-resolved scattering contrast is (C_sca,+ − C_sca,−)/(C_sca,+ + C_sca,−). Label it scattering contrast, not absorption circular dichroism. Absorption contrast is undefined when its denominator vanishes.

  1. A minimal native “Improve” objective

Use a fixed exterior target and fixed incident plane wave:

[ J=|E_{\rm incident}(r_)+E_{\rm scattered}(r_)|^2. ]

In vacuum the incident wave has unit electric-field norm, so this also gives intensity enhancement.

A one-shot objective-and-gradient binding is simplest:

cluster_ctx = tmatrix::cluster(lmax, k0, radii, epsilon, positions)
(a, incident_ctx) = plane::expansion(basis, [k], [helicity], true)
T = cluster_ctx.value()
b = T a
field_ctx = fields::field(basis, b, [target], [k0,k0], true, Outgoing)

E = direct_incident(target) + field_ctx.value[0]
J = sum(abs(E)^2)

field_grad = field_ctx.pullback([2 E])
g_b = field_grad.coefficients
g_T = g_b a†
g_a = T† g_b

incident_grad = incident_ctx.pullback(g_a, true)
cluster_grad = cluster_ctx.pullback(g_T)

g_radii = cluster_grad.radii
g_positions = cluster_grad.positions
            + incident_grad.origins
            + field_grad.origins

The three position terms are essential: mutual scattering, incident phase, and radiation origin motion. fixed_vectors=true still computes origin gradients; it suppresses wavevector derivatives.

All three pullbacks consume their residuals. Compute g_T and g_a before consuming cluster_ctx. Current ScatteringSystem discards its cluster residual, so a fresh one-shot evaluation for each optimization step avoids introducing a retained-context API into the cached visualization object.

Keep frequency, illumination and target fixed during a shape step. Enforce positive bounded radii, nonoverlap, and target clearance before accepting a trial. If the target follows a particle, or the objective includes a changing normalization, additional analytic chain-rule terms are required.

No files changed or builds run.
